comparator.name: Bachelor Bedrijfskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026-27 programme page states a 180-EC part-time bachelor of 110 EC compulsory subject courses, 25 EC academic skills, 30 EC free space and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. The 2026-27 annual schedule (jaarrooster) lists the 22 compulsory 5-EC subject courses, the three academic-skills courses (Basic Academic Skills 5 EC, Methods and Techniques of Research 15 EC, Methods and Techniques of Research 2 5 EC), the thesis (15 EC) and six 5-EC free-space slots, which total exactly 180 EC. The programme has no formal routes or specializations; its learning lines (strategic management, organisation and HRM, accounting and finance, marketing and supply chain management, resilient business, leadership of transitions, methods and techniques of research) organise the compulsory courses. The six free-space slots are preserved as open elective space and not filled with invented content. The schedule's footnotes cite two course codes (MB2502, MB2202) that differ by one digit from the table codes (MB2512, MB2212); the table codes were used. The programme-specific OER was not consulted because the page and schedule are consistent and sufficient.

alternatives.label: Business, management & organisation
alternatives.concept: A broad business-administration programme combining entrepreneurship and strategy with organisation and leadership, accounting, finance and economics, marketing and market research, research methods, business law and ethics, mirroring the integrated learning lines of the Open Universiteit bachelor as far as UCR's offering allows.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum spans management, entrepreneurship, leadership, finance, economics, marketing and research rather than one business subfield, so the label names business, management and organisation together.
progression: Business foundations (entrepreneurship, accounting, economics, research methods) precede advanced strategy, marketing, law, leadership and market research; all formal prerequisites occur in earlier semesters and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & quantitative business analysis
alternatives.concept: A programme organised around the accounting and finance learning line and the economics of the business environment, deepened with microeconomics, public and behavioural economics, econometrics, mathematics, probability, data science and machine learning for financial and economic analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has one accounting course and one finance course within a larger economics and quantitative-methods core, so the label names finance, economics and quantitative analysis rather than implying a full accounting-and-finance curriculum.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces the leadership, marketing, sustainability and law courses with a sequenced economics curriculum (intermediate micro, public and behavioural economics, econometrics) and a mathematics-statistics-data-science sequence, so the courses that differ follow from deepening finance and economic analysis.
progression: Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics and Linear Algebra; research methods and gateway economics precede intermediate economics, econometrics and market research; all formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Resilient & sustainable business, leadership & societal transitions
alternatives.concept: A programme organised around the resilient-business and leadership-of-transitions learning lines, combining entrepreneurship, strategy, leadership and organisational behaviour with sustainability, climate, circular-economy, governance and risk-adaptation study.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum pairs a business and leadership core with a substantial sustainability sequence, so the label names business, sustainability and societal transitions rather than implying a pure environmental programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match and the finance route, this route replaces economics, finance, marketing, law and quantitative methods with a sequenced Environment & Sustainability curriculum (Sustainability Essentials I and II, climate, circular economy, governance, renewable systems, hazards and adaptation) and societal-pressure courses, so the differing courses implement the transitions and resilience learning lines.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes the 300-level circular-economy and renewable-system courses; entrepreneurship and research foundations precede strategy, marketing and leadership; all formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

selection.assessment: Two further directions pass evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility after the closest match: finance and economics with quantitative analysis, and resilient and sustainable business with leadership of transitions. Each shares at most 15 courses with any other alternative, above the 30-EC floor. The marketing, customers and supply-chain direction was rejected as not-substantively-distinct: UCR has no supply-chain course and the few marketing and market-research courses it offers already sit in the closest match, so a marketing-led programme would differ only by arbitrary substitutions. Human-resource management is covered only through leadership and organisational-behaviour courses because UCR has no HRM course.

blocks: Both develop entrepreneurial business creation: venture idea, business model, market validation and pitch; the OU course is a broader entrepreneurship course within a management curriculum.
Both address organisational strategy: strategic planning from vision to execution; UCR adds a digital-transformation emphasis.
Both address the innovation process: UCR develops new products from customer needs to prototype, a specific part of innovation management rather than its full organisational scope.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course offers a comparable general introduction to management and organisation.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course addresses open innovation across organisational boundaries.
Both examine behaviour in organisations: motivation, group dynamics and organisational culture, using case-based analysis.
Both teach leadership theory and applied leadership practice; UCR emphasises personal leadership and self-awareness.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course gives a comparable organisation-theory treatment of structures and design.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no human-resource-management course.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no organisational advisory and coaching course.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no course on resilience and wellbeing in the workplace.
Both address marketing strategy, consumer behaviour and customer engagement.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR has no separate business-to-business marketing course beyond the general marketing course already matched to Marketing.
Both centre on reading and analysing financial statements and accounting information for business decisions.
Both develop corporate and personal financial decision-making: investment, budgeting and risk assessment.
Both introduce micro- and macroeconomics for understanding firms, markets and the wider economic environment.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no management-accounting course; its single accounting course is matched to Business Analysis and Reporting.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no sustainable-finance course.
Both teach research design, surveys and quantitative methods for empirical research; the OU course is a 15-EC practicum-based methods course with a wider scope.
Both develop applied empirical research: planning, collecting and analysing data and reporting findings.
Both address governance of business in a wider institutional setting: UCR through cross-border governance and corporate responsibility rather than corporate-governance structures alone.
UCR Ethics supplies the moral-theory foundations of business ethics; it is general ethics rather than ethics applied to business.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no supply-chain-management course.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: UCR offers no course on supply-chain resilience; life-cycle and circular-economy courses address a different question.
Both develop academic writing, critical use of sources and presenting skills at the start of the degree.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of entrepreneurship, strategy, marketing, accounting and finance, economics, leadership and organisational behaviour, research methods and business ethics. The Open Universiteit bachelor additionally includes compulsory courses in human resource management, supply chain management and supply-chain resilience, management accounting, sustainable finance, organisational consulting and coaching and open innovation, plus six free-space courses and a bachelor thesis. UCR students can instead combine leadership, finance, economics, sustainability and quantitative courses, but those specialist components are not offered as separate courses.
